scope: Independent EventBus dispatch and notification outbox workers
command: python3 -m pytest tests/test_event_worker_recovery.py tests/test_kernel_runtime_supervisor.py tests/test_core_features.py tests/test_scheduled_command_contracts.py tests/test_notification_outbox.py tests/test_worker_operation_map.py tests/test_worker_source_closure.py tests/test_worker_function_reachability.py tests/test_worker_sql_inventory.py tests/test_worker_sql_reachability.py tests/test_worker_boundary_preflight.py -q
focused_checks: The CLI exposes separate event-dispatch and notification-delivery worker modes while retaining --worker as the combined compatibility mode.
The event-only worker opens and closes the EventBus but does not open the notification database connection.
The notification-only worker claims and delivers outbox work without opening the EventBus.
The Kernel supervisor starts and disables event and notification children independently and gives each a unique identity.
Supervisor child worker-secret allowlists remain operation-specific; notification delivery does not receive a dedicated worker-secret allowance.
Long-running worker modes remain rejected by scheduled-command validation.
static_checks: Python compilation on changed Python files
Compose config for legacy worker, Kernel standard, and Kernel portability profiles
Capability matrix integrity (66 rows; MAN-CAP checks separately gated)

Kernel standard Compose flag matrix: default enables both workers, disabling the event bus disables notifications by inherited default, and explicit notification enablement runs the outbox worker independently.
limitations: Checks use mocks and static Compose parsing; no database, notification provider, candidate service, or legacy service was contacted.

The split isolates dispatch and delivery process responsibility, not database identity or provider credentials. Event handlers still use the shared runtime database identity and read destination configuration to decide which durable intents to enqueue.
Real provider delivery, populated workload parity, long-duration worker recovery, and MAN-CAP acceptance remain open.
